_doc: WHICH BACKEND DOES THE WORK. The coordinator is whichever model runs the /df-* commands;
the reviewer and the implementer are backends bound here, and they need not be the same one.
Keys beginning with _ are documentation for the human and for the coordinator reading this file.
They are never parameters. Everything else is.
Read this file at the start of every phase command: roles.<role> -> profiles.<id> -> adapter,
then load .claude/docs/adapters/<adapter>.md and nothing else. Schema and the adapter contract:
.claude/docs/adapters/_contract.md. Switch roles with /df-implementer, never by hand mid-run.

_fields.roles: Which profile plays each role. Same id twice = one backend does everything, exactly like a single-backend run.
_fields.profiles.<id>.adapter: Which adapter doc governs the mechanics: 'codex' or 'opencode'. The adapter is HOW to talk to it; the profile is WHICH model, with what limits.
_fields.profiles.<id>.label: Human line, shown in reports and the morning report.
_fields.profiles.<id>.verified: Has this profile passed /df-implementer --smoke on THIS machine? A profile that has never passed one is not usable in an unattended run. Set it true only after a smoke test actually returned a reply.
_fields.profiles.<id>.invoke: Adapter-specific launch parameters. See the adapter doc for how each key becomes a flag.
_fields.profiles.<id>.env_file: Path to a dotenv file to source before the call, or null. Secrets live there, never in this file.
_fields.profiles.<id>.env_required: Env vars that must be non-empty after sourcing env_file. Missing one = preflight failure, not a mysterious 401 at 3am.
_fields.profiles.<id>.capabilities: What the backend can actually do. The protocol branches on these — an honest 'false' here is worth more than an optimistic 'true'.
_fields.profiles.<id>.capabilities.edits_files: Can it write to the repo itself? False = it can only review; never send it an IMPLEMENT block.
_fields.profiles.<id>.capabilities.runs_commands: Can it run tests and lint? False = drop the TESTS: line from the required output and run everything yourself. You re-run them either way.
_fields.profiles.<id>.capabilities.sessions: Does context carry across calls? False = re-inline the spec and the prior round into every prompt.
_fields.profiles.<id>.capabilities.sandboxed: Are its writes confined to the target repo by the tool itself? False = nothing stops it touching the rest of the disk, so the prompt must forbid it and the diff review is the only net. Weigh this before pointing a backend at a machine with other work on it.
_fields.profiles.<id>.capabilities.network: Does it have network access? False = installs fail, so provision the environment yourself first and put the no-network block in every IMPLEMENT prompt.
_fields.profiles.<id>.capabilities.context_token: Usable context window. Drives work-package sizing in /df-plan and the prompt budget below. Set it to what the model is ACTUALLY loaded with, not its theoretical maximum — a 256k-capable model served at 32k is a 32k model.
_fields.profiles.<id>.limits.spec_review_rounds: Review rounds before /df-spec cuts the WP down to whatever the reviewer has no blockers against. Lower it for a weak reviewer: three rounds of vague objections is worse than one round and a smaller WP.
_fields.profiles.<id>.limits.fix_rounds: Verification fix rounds before the WP is handed to the fallback, or blocked.
_fields.profiles.<id>.limits.call_timeout_ms: Bash timeout for one call. Local models are slower than they look: a 30B model on a laptop can take 20+ minutes on a real work package.
_fields.profiles.<id>.limits.max_prompt_chars: Prompt budget, or null for none. A prompt over budget must be trimmed (drop the 'Already built' detail first, then narrow the PROJECT.md slice) or the WP split. Keep it near a third of the window in characters — the agent needs the rest of the context for the files it reads and the commands it runs.
_fields.profiles.<id>.preflight.check: Cheap shell command proving the backend is reachable BEFORE the night depends on it. Run by /df-implementer --smoke.
_fields.profiles.<id>.preflight.hint: What to tell the human when that check fails. For a local model this is usually 'the server is not running' or 'the model is not loaded'.
_fields.profiles.<id>.fallback: Profile id that takes over after fix_rounds are exhausted, or null for none. Default is null on purpose: a fallback quietly finishing the work is exactly what ruins a backend comparison. Turn it on for production nights, off for experiments.

_env: Secrets live in .env at the harness root (git-ignored; .env.example is the tracked template).
A profile naming an env_file expects the call to be made with it sourced:
Never paste a key into this file, a prompt, a WP log or a commit. Local backends need no key at all —
that is a real advantage of running a model on your own machine, not an afterthought.

codex-cloud.label: Codex CLI, hosted model, ChatGPT auth
codex-cloud._doc: The default and the only profile proven on this machine. Use it as the control when measuring anything else.

preflight.hint: codex login  — then re-run the smoke call

codex-lmstudio.label: Local model via LM Studio, driven by the Codex agent loop
codex-lmstudio._doc: Same agent loop, sandbox and sessions as codex-cloud; only the model changes. That is what makes it a clean experiment. Set invoke.model to the exact id `lms ls` prints, and context_tokens to the context length you loaded it with.

preflight.hint: lms server start, then lms load <model-id> — check the id with lms ls

codex-ollama.label: Local model via Ollama, driven by the Codex agent loop
codex-ollama._doc: As codex-lmstudio, against Ollama's OpenAI-compatible endpoint. invoke.model must match `ollama list` exactly, tag included.

preflight.hint: ollama serve, then ollama pull <model> — check what is installed with ollama list

codex-openrouter.label: OpenRouter model, driven by the Codex agent loop  [UNVERIFIED]
_doc: Reaches OpenRouter through a custom [model_providers.openrouter] entry in ~/.codex/config.toml;
the codex adapter doc, section 8, has the exact TOML. Unverified for a specific reason: OpenAI's
own config reference documents wire_api = 'responses' only, and OpenRouter serves the
chat-completions API. It may simply fail. Smoke-test it before trusting it, and if it fails that
way, use opencode-openrouter instead — OpenCode speaks OpenRouter natively.

preflight.hint: put OPENROUTER_API_KEY in .env and source it; add [model_providers.openrouter] to ~/.codex/config.toml per the codex adapter doc section 8

opencode-lmstudio.label: Local model via LM Studio, driven by OpenCode
opencode-lmstudio._doc: A second agent loop over the same local model. Run it against codex-lmstudio to separate what the MODEL cannot do from what the HARNESS-to-tool plumbing cannot do — the single most useful comparison on this list. Note capabilities.sandboxed: OpenCode has no workspace jail.

preflight.hint: install OpenCode (https://opencode.ai), then lms server start && lms load <model-id>

opencode-ollama.label: Local model via Ollama, driven by OpenCode
opencode-ollama._doc: As opencode-lmstudio, against Ollama. The model id after the provider prefix must match `ollama list`.

preflight.hint: install OpenCode (https://opencode.ai), then ollama serve && ollama pull <model>

opencode-openrouter.label: OpenRouter model, driven by OpenCode
opencode-openrouter._doc: The supported OpenRouter path: OpenCode has a first-class openrouter provider, so the key is all it needs. Useful for renting a frontier model for one night, or for pitting several models against the same backlog without installing anything. Change invoke.model to any OpenRouter model id.

preflight.hint: install OpenCode (https://opencode.ai) and put OPENROUTER_API_KEY in .env
